ux_interpretation.primary_user: Site Operator — whoever watches the IPS dashboard for a site and adjusts its anchors (role inferred from the RFQ; facility operations, airline IT, field engineer or demo presenter is still open)
ux_interpretation.user_goal: Trust that the floor shows exactly who is present now, explain any reading that looks wrong, and keep the anchors working without interrupting the people being tracked
ux_interpretation.business_goal: Demonstrate the IPS MVP's core value (accurate indoor location tied to a logged-in identity, plus live system status) to the airline example customer, while proving that the vendor platform never holds PII
ux_interpretation.main_task: Watch the live floor, drill from a suspicious marker to the reading and the anchor behind it, and recalibrate or update that anchor safely
ux_interpretation.context: An operations or demo setting on one site (the pilot is a single room with four corner anchors), often with the client watching. Positions update roughly every second. Names come from the customer's systems, never from the vendor's.
ux_interpretation.entry_point: 01 - Sign In through the customer's identity provider, landing on 02 - Live Floor
ux_interpretation.expected_outcome: The operator can say who is on the floor and where with confidence, can tell a bad reading from a bad anchor, and can change an anchor without anyone silently losing tracking
required_data: Live position and presence events per digital ID
Display names from the customer identity service
business_rules: Only logged-in devices are tracked and displayed (RFQ §4)
A user switching devices shows on the new device only (RFQ §4, §5D)
A user leaving coverage fades and is then removed, and returning restores them (RFQ §5D)
The IPS platform never holds PII; mapping from digital ID to person happens only on customer servers (RFQ ID Management)
The IPS Cloud ingests data only from the store computer (RFQ §3A, §4)
Anchor and store-computer configuration is viewable and modifiable from the dashboard (RFQ §4)
constraints: Overall latency target as stated in the RFQ ('between 1 seconds', bound to be confirmed)
SDK, store-computer software and anchor firmware are out of scope, so staged OTA and rollback depend on teams outside this RFQ
Web only for this stage; the demo phone app is not wireframed
dependencies: Customer identity provider for operator sign-in
Customer identity service exposing signed digital-ID resolution
Store computer streaming positions and equipment status

primary_journey: 01 - Sign In: operator signs in through the customer IdP; names policy and roles are loaded
02 - Live Floor: operator sees anchors and live people; system status chips are green
02 - Live Floor: a person's marker looks wrong; operator opens them
03 - Person Detail: verdict says only one anchor hears this phone strongly; signal chart shows Anchor NE weak for everyone
05 - Equipment Detail: drift card says phones near Anchor NE are placed 2.4 m off their neighbours' estimate
06 - Change Settings: editor adjusts calibration and checks the impact preview (3 phones, all covered by neighbours)
05 - Equipment Detail: calibration applied; snackbar offers revert
02 - Live Floor: the person's marker settles; operator returns to watching
supporting_tasks: Review site health and drift flags (04)
Run a staged firmware update and monitor it (06, 07)
Reveal one person's name with a reason under the anonymous-ID policy (03)
Find out how and when someone left the floor (08)
Search for one person on a busy floor (02)
error_scenarios: The store computer goes offline and markers freeze (02 error, 04 edge case)
The customer identity service is down and names degrade to anonymous IDs (01, 02, 03)
An anchor fails verification during a rollout, rolls back automatically and the rollout pauses (07 error)
An anchor disconnects mid-review of a settings change (06 error)
A person logs out while their detail sheet is open (03 empty)
Two editors change the same anchor (06 edge case)

pages.purpose: Authenticate the operator through the customer's identity provider, establish which site they may see, whether they may change equipment settings, and obtain the signed token the browser uses to resolve names from the customer's identity service.
content_structure: Product name and environment label (for example 'Pilot')
Sign-in panel: a single 'Sign in' button that hands off to the customer identity provider
Status line for the hand-off (redirecting, returning, failed)
Privacy line: 'This dashboard never stores who people are. Names are fetched from your organisation for this session only.'
pages.navigation: No app chrome. On success, routes to 02 - Live Floor for the operator's default site.

components.name: Component / Banner
components.why_new: Material 3 dropped the Material 2 banner but these pages need a persistent, page-level condition (positions frozen, names unavailable) that a transient snackbar cannot carry; rebuilt on the M2 banner anatomy with M3 colour and type tokens.

data: Operator identity and roles from the customer IdP (OIDC claims)
Permitted sites
Name-display policy for the operator's organisation (names on, or anonymous IDs with reveal)
interactions: Sign in redirects to the customer IdP and returns with a session
On return, the browser requests a signed identity-resolution token; failure to obtain it does not block sign-in, it degrades names to anonymous IDs

states.default: Centered card on md.sys.color.surface with the filled 'Sign in' button and the privacy line beneath.
states.loading: After return from the IdP the button is replaced by a linear progress bar labelled 'Opening your site…' while roles and the site list load.
states.empty: Operator authenticated but holds no site permission: card reads 'Your account isn't assigned to a site yet', names the customer administrator role to contact, and offers one action, 'Sign out'.
states.error: IdP hand-off failed or timed out: banner 'Sign-in didn't complete — your organisation's sign-in service didn't respond' with 'Try again'; nothing the operator typed is lost because nothing is typed here.
states.success: No interstitial; the operator lands on 02 - Live Floor and a snackbar confirms the site name.
states.disabled: While the hand-off is in flight the button shows the Loading variant and ignores repeat clicks, so a double-click cannot start two sessions.

responsive.desktop: Card 400px wide, centred vertically and horizontally on a md.sys.color.surface-container-low field.
responsive.laptop: Identical to desktop; the card does not scale with the viewport.
responsive.tablet: Card 400px, centred; the privacy line wraps to two lines.
responsive.mobile: Card goes full-bleed with md.sys.spacing.edge-margin side insets; button is full width and pinned above the keyboard-safe area.

accessibility.contrast: Button label md.sys.color.on-primary on md.sys.color.primary; privacy line md.sys.color.on-surface-variant on md.sys.color.surface checked at 4.5:1 or better because it is body-size text.
accessibility.keyboard_focus: Focus starts on 'Sign in'; Tab reaches 'Get help signing in' next. The focus ring is a 2px md.sys.color.primary outline offset by 2px, never suppressed on mouse use.
accessibility.labels: The button's accessible name is 'Sign in with your organisation', which is more specific than the visible label. The error banner names the failing service in words, not an error code.
accessibility.touch_targets: Sign-in button 48px tall at full card width; help link padded to a 44x44px hit area.
accessibility.reading_order: h1 product name, then the sign-in panel, then the privacy line. A single h1 and no other headings.
accessibility.status_messages: 'Opening your site…' and the sign-in failure are both set in an assertive live region, because each changes what the operator can do next and there is nothing else on the page to read.
accessibility.motion: Under prefers-reduced-motion the indeterminate progress bar is replaced by static text 'Opening your site…' with no sweep.

data_dependencies: Customer IdP OIDC authorize and token endpoints
POST /v1/sessions — IPS Cloud API (proposed): exchanges the IdP token for a dashboard session and returns roles + permitted sites
POST /v1/identity-tokens — IPS Cloud API (proposed): returns a short-lived token signed under the customer intermediate CA for browser-side name resolution
permissions: Any authenticated operator may sign in
Role 'equipment-editor' is read from IdP claims and governs 06 - Change Settings
edge_cases: Operator's IdP session is valid but the identity-token request fails: sign in succeeds, names degrade to anonymous IDs, and 02 shows the names-unavailable banner
Operator permitted on more than one site: lands on the most recently viewed site, switchable from the top bar
Clock skew between browser and token issuer rejects the signed token: retried once with server time, then degraded as above
open_questions: Which identity provider does the customer use, and will it carry an equipment-editor role claim?
Does the demo require a username/password form (the RFQ's 'JohnDoe / demo123' is the phone app, not the dashboard)?

pages.purpose: Show exactly who is present on the floor right now, where they are, and whether the system behind that picture is healthy, so the operator can trust or question the map at a glance.
content_structure: Top app bar: site selector, system status chips (store computer, anchors online n/N, stream heartbeat), operator menu
Page-level banner slot (positions frozen, names unavailable, drift suspected) shown only when a condition is active
Floor plan canvas: room outline, doors, anchor markers by status, person markers by presence state with name or anonymous ID
Right panel with tabs 'People | Raw stream': People is a searchable list (name or ID, presence state, nearest anchor, signal strength label); Raw stream is the live log
Legend explaining marker shapes (always visible, collapsible)
pages.navigation: Navigation rail destinations: Live floor (current), Site health, Activity. Selecting a person opens 03 - Person Detail as a side sheet over the floor; selecting an anchor or the store computer opens 05 - Equipment Detail.

components.name: Component / Banner
components.why_new: Material 3 dropped the Material 2 banner but these pages need a persistent, page-level condition (positions frozen, names unavailable) that a transient snackbar cannot carry; rebuilt on the M2 banner anatomy with M3 colour and type tokens.

components.name: Component / Floor Plan Canvas
components.why_new: No Material 3 component positions live objects on a scaled floor plan. Logged as a design-system gap.

components.name: Component / Presence Marker
components.why_new: Encodes presence state by shape and label, not colour: solid disc = live, dashed ring with last-seen age = fading, hatched disc = frozen. No M3 badge or avatar carries a time-based state. Logged as a design-system gap.

components.name: Component / Anchor Marker
components.why_new: An anchor's status needs four shape-distinct glyphs (filled triangle, outlined triangle with slash, triangle with exclamation, triangle with rotating arc) placed on the canvas; M3 icons are not stateful.

components.name: Component / Stream Log
components.why_new: The RFQ requires a raw streaming-data view. An append-only, pausable, monospace log with follow-tail semantics is not an M3 list. Logged as a design-system gap.

components.name: Component / Skeleton
components.why_new: Material 3 specifies loading indicators but no skeleton placeholder; built from md.sys.color.surface-container-high blocks at the loaded content's exact dimensions so layout never shifts.

data: Floor plan geometry and scale for the site
Anchor list with position, status, health, firmware, drift flag
Live position events per digital ID (timestamp, x, y, z, connected anchor, signal strength)
Presence state per digital ID derived from the site's fade and remove timings
Display names resolved in the browser from the customer identity service, or anonymous IDs
Store-computer connectivity and stream heartbeat status
interactions: Markers move as position events arrive; no animation longer than the update interval
Click or Enter on a marker or list row opens 03 for that person
Click or Enter on an anchor marker or the store-computer chip opens 05
'/' focuses people search; results filter the list and highlight matching markers
Tab 'Raw stream' swaps the people list for the stream log in the same panel, rather than adding a third column
Legend toggles open and closed; its state persists per operator

states.default: Floor plan fills the canvas with anchors at the four corners (pilot layout) and live markers; People tab lists everyone present, sorted by name or ID.
states.loading: Canvas shows the room outline from cached geometry with anchor markers as skeleton triangles, and the people list shows six skeleton rows. The top bar status chips read 'Connecting…' until the first live event arrives.
states.empty: Live data is flowing but nobody is logged in on this floor: the canvas shows anchors only, and the list reads 'Nobody is being tracked on this floor. People appear here when they sign in to the app.' Its one action is 'View recent activity' (to 08).
states.error: The store computer stops sending: every marker switches to the Frozen variant (hatched) at its last position, the list's presence column reads 'Frozen', and the banner reads 'Positions frozen since 10:42:07 — the store computer is offline. People may have moved.' Its action is 'View site health'. Markers are never left looking live on stale data.
states.disabled: When names cannot be resolved, the 'Reveal name' action elsewhere is unavailable and markers show anonymous IDs; the banner explains 'Names unavailable — your organisation's identity service isn't responding. Showing anonymous IDs.'

responsive.desktop: Navigation rail 80px, canvas flexible, right panel 360px fixed with People and Raw stream tabs; legend docked bottom-left of the canvas.
responsive.laptop: Same structure as desktop with the right panel at 320px and tighter md.sys.spacing.edge-margin.
responsive.tablet: Rail stays, the right panel collapses into a standard bottom sheet peeking 96px (count of people present), and the canvas takes the full width; dragging the sheet up reveals the list.
responsive.mobile: Rail becomes a modal navigation drawer behind a menu icon. A segmented button 'Map | List' leads the page and defaults to List: rows show name or ID, presence state and nearest anchor. Map is full-bleed with pinch and zoom, and the raw stream moves to 03 only.

accessibility.contrast: Marker labels md.sys.color.on-surface on md.sys.color.surface-container-lowest canvas at 4.5:1 or better; marker outlines and anchor glyphs md.sys.color.outline against the canvas at 3:1 or better as non-text UI. Presence and anchor status are encoded by shape plus a text label, never colour alone.
accessibility.keyboard_focus: Tab order is top bar, then banner action, then canvas, then right panel tabs, then list. Inside the canvas, arrow keys move between objects in reading order (anchors first by label, then people by name), Enter opens, and Escape returns focus to the canvas container. The focus ring is a 2px md.sys.color.primary outline around the marker's 48px hit area.
accessibility.labels: Each marker's accessible name states the person, state and nearest anchor, for example 'Person 7F3A, live, nearest Anchor NE, signal good'. The canvas has a text alternative: 'Floor plan, DN-20 Atrium, 4 anchors, 3 people present.' The search field has a visible label 'Search people'.
accessibility.touch_targets: Person and anchor markers have 48x48px hit areas regardless of drawn size; list rows 56px tall; status chips 32px tall inside a 48px hit area.
accessibility.reading_order: h1 is the site and floor name (visually in the top bar), h2 'Floor plan', h2 'People' / 'Raw stream'. The DOM order matches the visual order and has no skipped levels.
accessibility.status_messages: People arriving or leaving are summarised in a polite live region at most every 10 seconds ('2 people arrived, 1 left'), so the operator is not interrupted per event. Positions freezing and names becoming unavailable are announced assertively once, because they change what every marker means.
accessibility.motion: Under prefers-reduced-motion markers jump to new positions instead of gliding, the fading state uses a static dashed ring instead of a pulse, and skeleton shimmer is replaced by flat placeholder blocks.

data_dependencies: GET /v1/sites/{siteId}/anchors — IPS Cloud API (proposed): position, status, health, firmware, drift flag
WS /v1/sites/{siteId}/live — IPS Cloud API (proposed): position and presence events for logged-in digital IDs only
POST /v1/resolve — Customer identity service (customer-hosted, proposed): digital IDs to display names, called from the browser with the signed token; never proxied through IPS
GET /v1/sites/{siteId}/stream-health — IPS Cloud API (proposed): store-computer last-seen, heartbeat interval, subscriber count
permissions: Any operator on the site may view
Names are shown only when the organisation policy and the identity service both allow; otherwise anonymous IDs
edge_cases: Same person logs in on a second phone before the first logs out: one marker only, on the newest device; the activity timeline records the switch
A person is between anchors and the stream lags past the latency bound: the marker enters Fading rather than snapping
Floor plan geometry is missing for a new site: the canvas is replaced by the list view with a banner asking an administrator to upload the plan
Over 200 people present: markers cluster by anchor with a count badge, and the list stays complete
WebSocket reconnects: positions are re-synced from a snapshot before deltas resume, so no ghost markers remain
open_questions: What are the fade and remove timings? The RFQ says 'progressively' and 'eventually' without numbers
Is the latency bound 1 second end-to-end? The RFQ text is garbled ('between 1 seconds')
Should the map default to names or anonymous IDs on a shared screen in an operations room?

pages.purpose: Explain one person's position: which anchor they are connected to, how strong the signal is, which other anchors hear them, the raw readings behind the marker and their recent presence history, so the operator can decide whether the reading or the anchor is at fault.
content_structure: Header: name or anonymous ID, presence state with last-seen age, current coordinates
Verdict line: 'Reading looks consistent' or 'Only one anchor hears this phone — position is approximate'
Connected anchor card: anchor label, signal strength label with dBm secondary
Signal strength chart: per hearing anchor, last 10 minutes, with a 'Show as table' toggle
Raw readings: the stream log filtered to this digital ID
Recent presence events for this person (last 30 minutes)
pages.navigation: Opens as a side sheet over 02 on desktop and laptop, and as a full page on tablet and mobile with a back arrow. 'Open nearest anchor' goes to 05 carrying this person as context.

components.name: Component / Signal Strength Chart
components.why_new: Material 3 has no charts. A small line chart of signal strength per hearing anchor over the last 10 minutes, with a data-table equivalent.

components.name: Component / Stream Log
components.why_new: The RFQ requires a raw streaming-data view. An append-only, pausable, monospace log with follow-tail semantics is not an M3 list. Logged as a design-system gap.

components.name: Component / Skeleton
components.why_new: Material 3 specifies loading indicators but no skeleton placeholder; built from md.sys.color.surface-container-high blocks at the loaded content's exact dimensions so layout never shifts.

components.name: Component / Banner
components.why_new: Material 3 dropped the Material 2 banner but these pages need a persistent, page-level condition (positions frozen, names unavailable) that a transient snackbar cannot carry; rebuilt on the M2 banner anatomy with M3 colour and type tokens.

data: Digital ID, display name if resolved
Presence state and last-seen timestamp
Current x, y, z
Connected anchor and signal strength
Signal strength per hearing anchor over 10 minutes
Raw stream rows for this digital ID
Presence events for this digital ID
interactions: 'Open nearest anchor' routes to 05 with this person highlighted in the anchor's connected-phones list
'Reveal name' (only under the anonymous-ID policy) opens a dialog asking for a reason from a short list plus free text; on confirm the name shows for this session and the reveal is logged
'Pause raw readings' freezes the log so rows can be read; a 'Resume' replaces it
'Show as table' swaps the chart for a data table of the same series

states.default: Header, verdict line, connected anchor card, chart with one line per hearing anchor, the last 50 raw rows, and presence events.
states.loading: Header renders immediately from the live state already on 02. The chart area shows a skeleton block of the chart's height, and the raw log and events show four skeleton rows each.
states.empty: The person logged out while the sheet was open: content dims and a banner reads 'This person signed out at 10:51:22 and is no longer tracked.' Its one action is 'Back to floor'. No data for a logged-out person stays visible.
states.error: Telemetry history failed to load: the chart area reads 'Signal history didn't load — live readings are still shown below' with 'Retry'. Header and raw log stay live.
states.success: After a reveal, a snackbar reads 'Name shown for this session. Your reveal was recorded.' and the header updates in place.
states.disabled: 'Reveal name' is disabled with the helper text 'Names are unavailable while your organisation's identity service is down' when resolution has failed, and hidden entirely when the policy already shows names.

responsive.desktop: Side sheet 480px wide over the floor plan, which stays visible and keeps the person's marker highlighted.
responsive.laptop: Side sheet 440px; the chart's height drops from 200px to 160px.
responsive.tablet: Full page with a top app bar and back arrow. The connected anchor card and verdict sit side by side above the chart.
responsive.mobile: Full page, single column: header, verdict, anchor card, then the chart defaults to the table view. The raw log is collapsed behind 'Show raw readings'.

accessibility.contrast: Verdict text md.sys.color.on-surface on md.sys.color.surface-container-low at 4.5:1 or better; chart lines are distinguished by md.sys.color.primary, md.sys.color.tertiary and md.sys.color.secondary plus distinct line dashes and end labels, each at 3:1 or better against the chart surface.
accessibility.keyboard_focus: When the sheet opens, focus moves to its heading. Tab runs primary action, reveal, chart toggle, log pause, then events. Escape closes the sheet and returns focus to the marker or row that opened it. The reveal dialog traps focus and returns it to 'Reveal name'.
accessibility.labels: Signal strength is shown as words ('Good', 'Fair', 'Weak') with dBm as secondary text, so the label works for an operator who isn't RF-literate. The reveal reason is a required labelled field whose error 'Choose a reason to reveal this name' sits below it.
accessibility.touch_targets: All buttons are at least 40px tall inside 48x48px hit areas; chart data points are not targets, and the table view is the interactive equivalent.
accessibility.reading_order: h2 person heading (the sheet is a region within 02's h1), h3 'Connection', h3 'Signal history', h3 'Raw readings', h3 'Recent activity'.
accessibility.status_messages: The verdict line is a polite live region and announces only when the verdict changes. New raw rows are not announced individually; pausing announces 'Raw readings paused at 10:52:03'. Sign-out while the sheet is open is assertive, because the content is no longer valid.
accessibility.motion: Under prefers-reduced-motion the sheet appears without a slide, and chart lines redraw without easing.

data_dependencies: GET /v1/sites/{siteId}/devices/{digitalId}/telemetry?window=10m — IPS Cloud API (proposed): signal strength per hearing anchor
GET /v1/sites/{siteId}/stream?digitalId={id}&limit=50 — IPS Cloud API (proposed): raw rows
POST /v1/resolve — Customer identity service (customer-hosted, proposed): on reveal
POST /v1/audit/reveals — IPS Cloud API (proposed): records operator, digital ID, reason, timestamp; stores no name
permissions: Any operator may view a person's telemetry
Reveal is available to any operator under the anonymous-ID policy and is always logged
edge_cases: Only one anchor hears the phone: verdict states the position is approximate rather than showing false precision
The person switches device while the sheet is open: the sheet follows the person to the new device and the events list shows the switch
Telemetry history exists only from the last reconnect: the chart starts at that point with a 'No data before 10:40' marker
Reveal requested while the identity service is down: blocked with the disabled explanation, never queued
open_questions: Is a logged reason for revealing a name acceptable to the customer's works council or privacy office, or is a stricter policy needed?
How long should a reveal last: this session, or until the person next logs out?

pages.purpose: Show at a glance whether every anchor, the store computer and the outbound customer stream are working, and surface anchors the system suspects are drifting before an operator notices bad readings.
content_structure: Summary cards: store computer (connected, last data received), anchors online (n of N), drift suspected (count), customer stream (heartbeat last sent, subscribers connected)
Active rollout strip if a staged update is running (links to 07)
Equipment table: label, type, status, health, firmware, connected phones, drift flag, last seen
pages.navigation: Rail destination 'Site health'. A row or summary card opens 05 - Equipment Detail. The rollout strip opens 07 - Rollout Progress.

components.why_new: Material 3 ships no data table; anchors and events are multi-column comparable data. Built from M3 list-row anatomy, md.sys.typescale.body-medium and md.sys.color.outline-variant row dividers.

components.name: Component / Anchor Marker

data: Store-computer connectivity and last data timestamp
Per anchor: status, health, firmware version, connected-phone count, drift flag and evidence summary, last seen
Stream health: heartbeat interval, last heartbeat sent, connected subscribers
Active rollout summary
interactions: Filter chips 'Offline', 'Drift suspected', 'Updating' narrow the table
Sort by any column
Row click or Enter opens 05
The rollout strip opens 07

states.default: Four summary cards over a table of five rows for the pilot (four anchors and one store computer), sorted with problems first.
states.loading: Summary cards show skeleton values with their labels already rendered, and the table shows five skeleton rows at final row height.
states.empty: A site with no equipment registered: the table area reads 'No equipment registered for this site yet. Anchors appear once the store computer reports them.' Its one action is 'View setup guide'.
states.error: Health data unavailable: the banner reads 'Equipment status couldn't be loaded — last known status from 10:38 is shown'. Values are shown with a 'Last known' label and the table stays usable.
states.disabled: When no rollout is active the rollout strip is absent rather than disabled, so there is nothing to explain.

responsive.desktop: Four summary cards in one row, with a full-width data table below and all eight columns.
responsive.laptop: Four cards in one row, and the 'last seen' column collapses into the status cell's secondary line.
responsive.tablet: Cards in a 2x2 grid. The table keeps label, status, drift and phones; the other columns move to a row-expansion panel.
responsive.mobile: Cards stack as a single column of compact rows, and the table recomposes to a list. Each item shows label, status glyph with text, and drift flag, and tapping it opens 05.

accessibility.contrast: Status text md.sys.color.on-surface on md.sys.color.surface at 4.5:1 or better; the 'Offline' and 'Drift suspected' treatments use md.sys.color.on-error-container on md.sys.color.error-container plus a distinct glyph and the word itself.
accessibility.keyboard_focus: Tab order is summary cards left to right, then filter chips, then table. In the table, arrow keys move between cells in grid mode and Enter on a row opens 05. The focus ring wraps the whole row.
accessibility.labels: The table has a caption 'Equipment on DN-20 Atrium' and column headers marked as headers. The drift flag cell reads 'Drift suspected: readings differ from neighbours', not just an icon.
accessibility.touch_targets: Table rows 52px tall, filter chips 32px tall inside 48px hit areas, and summary cards fully clickable at a minimum of 96px tall.
accessibility.reading_order: h1 'Site health', h2 'Summary', h2 'Equipment'. The rollout strip, when present, sits between them as an h2 'Update in progress'.
accessibility.status_messages: An anchor going offline or a new drift flag is announced politely ('Anchor SW went offline'), throttled to one summary per 15 seconds. The store computer disconnecting is assertive.
accessibility.motion: There is no decorative motion. Under prefers-reduced-motion the rollout strip's progress bar updates in steps rather than animating.

data_dependencies: GET /v1/sites/{siteId}/drift — IPS Cloud API (proposed): per-anchor drift flag with evidence summary
WS /v1/sites/{siteId}/equipment-events — IPS Cloud API (proposed): status changes
permissions: Any operator on the site may view
edge_cases: Store computer offline: anchor statuses become 'Unknown since 10:42' rather than staying 'Online', because they report through it
An anchor reports a firmware version no rollout has issued: flagged 'Unexpected firmware'
Drift check has under 10 minutes of data after a restart: flag column reads 'Checking…' rather than 'OK'
Customer stream has zero subscribers: the stream card reads 'No customer system is listening' as a warning, not an error
open_questions: What does 'health' measure beyond online/offline? The RFQ requires it but does not define it
Should drift detection alert anyone, or only display? Notifications are out of MVP scope in the RFQ

pages.purpose: Show everything about one anchor or the store computer — status, health, firmware, the phones connected to it, and the drift evidence — so the operator can decide whether it needs recalibration or an update.
content_structure: Header: equipment label and type, status with text, firmware version, last seen
Context chip if arriving from 03: 'From Person 7F3A' with that person highlighted below

Connected phones list: name or ID, signal strength label, time connected
Current settings summary (read-only)
Setting history: last five changes with who, when and a revert action
pages.navigation: Breadcrumb 'Site health › Anchor NE'. 'Change settings' opens 06. 'View on floor' returns to 02 with this anchor selected.

interactions: 'Change settings' opens 06 for this equipment (shown only to equipment editors)

states.default: Header, drift card (if flagged; otherwise a one-line 'Readings agree with neighbouring anchors'), connected phones, settings summary, history.

pages.purpose: Let an equipment editor change calibration settings or start a firmware update with a clear preview of who is affected, and with a rollout plan that keeps every tracked person covered.

Rollout plan (firmware only): staged by default, one anchor at a time while neighbours cover; 'All at once' available only when nobody is present
Review step: summary of change, impact, plan; 'Apply' confirm
pages.navigation: Breadcrumb 'Site health › Anchor NE › Change settings'. 'Cancel' returns to 05 without changes. A firmware apply lands on 07; a calibration apply returns to 05 with a success snackbar.

design_system_gaps.need: A scaled floor plan on which live person markers and anchor markers are positioned by (x, y), panned and zoomed, and navigable by keyboard as an ordered list of objects
design_system_gaps.why_insufficient: A chart plots data on axes. This is a spatial map of a real room, where position is the content, objects are interactive, and a non-visual user needs an equivalent structure ('3 people near Anchor NE').

design_system_gaps.need: A person marker whose state is time-based (live, fading with a last-seen age, frozen when upstream data stops) and readable without colour
design_system_gaps.why_insufficient: A badge is a static count or dot. It has no notion of time since last update, and its states are colour-coded by convention.

design_system_gaps.need: A live append-only log with follow-tail, pause, and filter-to-one-device, whose updates must not flood assistive technology
design_system_gaps.why_insufficient: A list renders a stable set of rows. A log grows several times a second, needs a paused or following mode, and needs announcements throttled to a summary rather than one per row.

heuristic_review.finding: When the store computer stopped sending, markers would stay where they were and still look live. An operator would read a frozen floor as people standing still, which is the 'show only who is really there' failure in its worst form.
heuristic_review.fix: Added a Frozen marker variant (hatched) that every marker switches to on store-computer loss, a banner stating the freeze time, and an assertive announcement. Anchor statuses on 04 become 'Unknown since…' for the same reason. Spec updated on 02 (error state, components) and 04 (edge cases).

heuristic_review.heuristic: Match between system and the real world
heuristic_review.finding: The first draft labelled signal as 'RSSI −71 dBm' and the person as 'digital ID'. That is the data model's vocabulary, and the operator role is not known to be RF-literate.
heuristic_review.fix: Signal is now shown as 'Good / Fair / Weak' with dBm as secondary text, the ID is labelled 'Anonymous ID', and a verdict sentence states in plain words whether the reading looks consistent. Spec updated on 03 (content structure, labels).

heuristic_review.finding: Once a firmware update started there was no way to stop it, and a calibration change had no way back. These are the two most expensive actions in the product, on live hardware with people being tracked.
heuristic_review.fix: Added 'Pause rollout' and 'Stop and roll back' on 07 (stop confirms, with the safe option focused), an automatic pause when an anchor fails verification, and setting history with per-change revert on 05. Spec updated on 05 and 07.

heuristic_review.finding: The draft had a map-wide 'Show names' toggle on 02 and a per-person 'Reveal name' on 03: two controls with near-identical names and very different scope and privacy consequences.
heuristic_review.fix: Removed the map-wide toggle. Whether names show by default is an organisation policy read at sign-in, and the only operator control is per-person 'Reveal name' on 03, which asks for a reason and is logged. Spec updated on 02 and 03.

heuristic_review.finding: A firmware update could be applied to every anchor at once while people were on the floor, taking the whole floor dark. Nothing in the flow prevented it.
heuristic_review.fix: Rollout defaults to staged (one anchor at a time while neighbours cover), and 'All at once' is disabled whenever anyone is present. Any change that leaves a phone uncovered needs an acknowledgement naming the people and the duration. Spec updated on 06.

heuristic_review.finding: An operator who suspected a person's reading on 03 and went to the anchor on 05 had to remember which person they were checking in order to find them in the connected-phones list.
heuristic_review.fix: Navigation from 03 to 05 carries the person as context: a 'From Person 7F3A' chip, with that person highlighted in the list, or a note that they have moved to another anchor. Spec updated on 05 (content structure, edge cases).

heuristic_review.finding: Finding one person on a busy floor meant scanning the map or scrolling the list, with no fast path for an operator doing it repeatedly.
heuristic_review.fix: Added people search focused by '/', which filters the list and highlights matching markers, plus arrow-key navigation between canvas objects. Spec updated on 02 (interactions, keyboard focus).

heuristic_review.finding: The draft gave the raw stream a third column beside the map and the people list, so the busiest page carried three live-updating regions competing for attention.
heuristic_review.fix: The raw stream now shares the right panel with People as a tab, and is filtered per person on 03, where it answers a question rather than scrolling for its own sake. Spec updated on 02 (content structure, interactions).

heuristic_review.heuristic: Help users recognize, diagnose and recover from errors
heuristic_review.finding: When names failed to resolve, an operator could not tell whether they lacked permission or the customer's identity service was down. Both looked like anonymous IDs.
heuristic_review.fix: A banner names the cause ('your organisation's identity service isn't responding'), sign-in degrades rather than failing when the token cannot be issued, and 'Reveal name' is disabled with the same explanation. Spec updated on 01 (edge cases), 02 (disabled state) and 03 (disabled state).

The two concepts that need explaining explain themselves in place: presence states carry a text label and last-seen age plus an always-available legend on 02, and the drift flag on 05 states its evidence and the usual remedy in one sentence. No separate help is needed for the primary journey.

assumptions: Design system: none was supplied, so the documented Material 3 baseline is used (human decision at the fork). Token names come from ux-pipeline/skills/wireframe-ia/references/material-design-tokens.json. Where Material 3 lacks a component (data table, breadcrumb, banner, skeleton, stepper, charts) it is built from M3 anatomy and tokens and marked new.

Direction: B+C composite. From B: one dashboard, names resolved in the operator's browser, pseudonymous fallback with per-person reveal, the reading-explainer panel, the impact preview and role-gated settings. From C: drift check, staged OTA with rollback, the presence/activity timeline, and the stream heartbeat (surfaced on 04 and 08).

The integration health panel (A-only) is not in this composite. The integrator persona's HMW 5 is served only by the heartbeat, which the customer's own monitoring consumes, and has no integrator UI here.
Every API endpoint named in data_dependencies is a proposal. The RFQ defines no API surface.
The operator role is the RFQ's unnamed 'users'. Two capabilities are assumed: view (all operators) and 'equipment-editor' (change settings, run rollouts), read from the customer IdP.
Whether names show by default is an organisation policy ('names on' or 'anonymous IDs with reveal') read at sign-in, not an operator toggle.
Single site per view, with a site selector in the top bar because the PKI design implies several sites. The pilot layout is one room with four corner anchors and two doors (RFQ p.6 mock-up).
Fade and remove timings for out-of-range people are configurable per site. The RFQ gives no values, so none are specified.
The demo phone app (login, welcome, config download) is not wireframed: target surface is web, and the app sits with the out-of-scope SDK.
The '90 seconds' OTA duration in 06's acknowledgement copy is a placeholder until real per-anchor update times are known.

ux: Primary journey walks 01 → 02 → 03 → 05 → 06 → 05 → 02 without dead ends

Every RFQ dashboard requirement (§4 dashboard, device tracking, streaming view; §5C) maps to a page: floor plan with anchors (02), status and health (02, 04), click to configure (05, 06), logged-in only (02), identity + coordinates + anchor + signal (02, 03), anchor's phones (05), raw stream (02, 03)
All five RFQ §5D scenarios have a defined visible behaviour on 02
